Instructions: Single operating checklist from discovery through ongoing SEO. Version 5.0, verified 2026-09-11. See the version history and Sources for the scope and dates of individual changes.

Resolve the release scope and conditional gate decisions first. Complete applicable Phase 0–4 gates and current evidence to reach READY FOR CUTOVER. Obtain and record owner authorization before cutover. Run applicable Phase 5 production checks after cutover; final GO requires their current evidence too. Record the human decision in 5.7. Phases 6–7 remain post-launch work.

Priority describes expected impact and urgency: P0 critical, P1 important, P2 lower impact/urgency. It does not set lifecycle, applicability or launch gating. An important optional enhancement can be P1; an applicable gate remains binding even if its Priority is P2.

Yes = active and counted. No = excluded through a reasoned scope decision. Review = decide whether the stated condition matches the actual site, business model, assets and chosen features. Resolve every conditional launch gate before cutover; a failed requirement is not grounds for a non-applicability exclusion.

Launch gate? identifies a dependency of this project's approved release policy, not a list of Google ranking factors or minimum indexing requirements. Each applicable gate must meet its stage-specific criterion with current evidence/history; resolve conditional applicability and exclusions first. Priority, Profile and purpose labels never override a gate.

Maintain the five existing Status values as the current task workflow. The calculated Last review UTC, Latest review result, Next review UTC and Review state columns show recorded observations and freshness. Append review history before marking Passed. Reconcile Status/Evidence with the latest outcome. Failed, Reopened, overdue or ambiguous history cannot satisfy an applicable gate; Skipped (N/A) cannot satisfy one either.

For each applicable Passed gate, maintain a release-specific evidence record with criterion, environment, date/time, tester, result, evidence reference and reviewer. Match the Checklist Evidence reference to that record. For every excluded gate, record and approve the non-applicability reason in the release scope. Blank or stale evidence keeps the gate incomplete; Profile and Priority do not waive evidence. Release context and registers are on Release review; record and verify UTC for each decision. Archive the signed dossier before a new release. Retain review runs in the ReviewRuns table on Release review; its row position can change when the control inventory expands. A Passed gate needs a latest current review matching all of its gate-test and reviewer fields, plus a next review UTC or named event trigger. Log relevant changes/incidents as Reopened; append retests without replacing prior runs. Freshness is evaluated at the explicitly updated Assessment UTC.

Leave Due date blank until work is scheduled. Once an owner commits to a dated task, record its due date. Use an actual whole calendar date, displayed yyyy-mm-dd, from 2020-01-01 through 2099-12-31; this is the maintained template's supported scheduling range. Overdue means an applicable unfinished scheduled task is before the recorded Assessment UTC date. Refresh Assessment UTC when reviewing the plan. Review-history freshness is assessed separately. Dates and their colours do not themselves make a launch gate pass.

Read both calculated assessments and their blocker diagnostics. READY FOR CUTOVER is preflight readiness; final GO requires completed live checks and a valid cutover record. Neither result itself records human authorization. Use 5.7 for the final owner decision.
International, migration, facets, pagination, non-HTML, ecommerce, local, analytics/consent, schema and AI rows now appear in their real lifecycle phases rather than a separate final phase.
This workbook prompts scope and evidence decisions; it is not legal advice or compliance certification. Use qualified review for privacy, consent, consumer and accessibility obligations.

The Sources sheet contains dated primary URLs used for time-sensitive technical and legal wording. Recheck them when platform behavior or law changes.

For gate review, show every Launch gate?=Yes row, including Review decisions and recorded exclusions, plus input-error rows; optionally show active Core work. Never use a Profile-only or Applies?=Yes-only filter to determine the gate inventory.

The original columns A:Q retain their order. Calculated review history fields occupy R:U. Filter the complete table and keep each row together; never sort only selected input columns. The review log is linked by control ID, not row position.

Deleted the broken Progress row that produced seven formula errors and repointed the launch-readiness formulas. Removed leftover v3 status validation and colour rules from the Due date column and the duplicate priority rule on C2:C55. Corrected four stale cross-references in Notes (1.4, 1.8, 3.5, 3.9). Rewrote 0.6 after verifying that the Search Console generative AI control does exist.

Closed remaining coverage gaps without changing the three-axis gating model. Added domain-renewal continuity, favicon/site-name identity, SEO-safe experimentation, video, paywall/gated content, publisher Discover/Preferred Sources and UGC/third-party-content modules. Refined URL conventions, image/search previews, Search Console associations, FAQ deprecation wording, AI reporting rollout wording and authorship/date scope. Clarified that Core filtering must never hide launch gates.

Narrowed AI-control language and clarified llms.txt; added a conditional breadcrumb/BreadcrumbList control; expanded domain-variant migration, review-integrity and internal-search handling; removed the partial Core-only launch-gate metric; and restored readable row heights. The gate model itself is unchanged.

Notes label each control's purpose: indexing/discovery; relevance/ranking consideration; search-feature eligibility; measurement; legal/accessibility; security/governance; or optional enhancement. Multiple labels identify distinct outcomes. These labels explain why the work exists; they do not change Priority, Applies?, Launch gate?, Status or Profile.

Google's minimum technical eligibility concerns crawl access, a working 200 response and indexable content, including spam-policy compliance. Meeting them does not guarantee indexing. This operating checklist also contains business, legal, accessibility and reliability dependencies. A release gate can protect those outcomes without being a ranking factor. Scope optional products/features deliberately; do not require analytics, a sitemap, a particular schema type, SSR or two Search Console owners merely for basic indexing. Sources: Google technical requirements; Search Essentials.

Relevance/ranking consideration identifies work related to useful content, links or relevant page experience; it does not mean every listed practice is an independently scored factor. Google uses Core Web Vitals in ranking, but lab budgets, analytics, consent, accessibility assessments and governance records are not themselves ranking scores. Structured-data rules govern chosen feature eligibility, with no guaranteed display. Keep private-data exposure, misleading shipped markup and other applicable release defects blocking; adoption of an optional feature remains a separate choice. Sources: Page experience and ranking; Structured-data guidelines.

Only a designated maintainer changes the control inventory. Save a new version, retain the signed prior release dossier and assign a new scope revision before adding a control. Clear the prior scope approval and cutover authorization records. A previous approval never automatically covers an added requirement. Keep previous review runs intact.

Unprotect the relevant sheets for maintenance. Insert or append a whole Checklist table row, using a unique text ID and an appropriate existing row as the format/formula template. Complete the original A:Q fields; preserve the calculated R:U columns. Add the same ID, phase, gate, applicability, criterion and evidence class to ReleaseScope and the protected fixed ID inventory. Add a GateEvidence record for a gate. Copy input validation, formulas and protection deliberately; do not copy another control's evidence or approval.

Before extending either release register, insert a whole worksheet row immediately below that register to move the sections below it safely. Confirm the actual named-table bounds after each insertion. Extend the fixed ID inventory and its identity-error formula. Update the expected control and gate counts and the fixed inventory range in Progress B22:B26 and B28 from the revised approved inventory. Keep those expected counts fixed; do not replace them with counts calculated from the same tables being checked.

Extend every affected dropdown, date rule, conditional format and input-integrity check through the new rows. Confirm that ReviewRuns offers the new ID and that its latest result appears on the matching Checklist row. Test the changed inventory in a disposable copy: applicable Failed and unresolved Review gates must HOLD, and complete current evidence must allow the appropriate stage to pass. Sort and filter whole tables, then save and reopen. Check the sections and long text visually, and re-protect the maintained sheets.

Never reuse an old control ID for a different requirement or delete historic review runs to improve readiness. Record any retirement or criterion change in the approved scope and version history. Retain prior evidence under its original release, scope and criterion. A new version of the inventory needs a fresh scope decision and matching current evidence before launch acceptance.

Orders01–15 implement two-stage readiness, release-specific evidence, current review history, clarified SEO/platform requirements, purpose classification and controlled inventory additions. Order16 adds consistent presentation, exact status formatting, scheduling validation and retained source/change history. The final verification report records acceptance and method-specific limits.

Use the workbook on screen. Checklist freezes its header, ID and phase; horizontal scrolling reveals the remaining fields. Navigate lower release registers by their table names ReleaseScope, GateEvidence and ReviewRuns using the Name Box. Filter and sort whole tables. The full21-column Checklist is not a supported one-page print. Print selected legible sections with repeated ID/phase and headers, then inspect page breaks. AutoFit and inspect rows after entering long evidence or trigger text.

Source IDs stay with exact URLs after sorting. Sources preserves verification dates, recorded verifier and next-review trigger; historical-only references are labelled and do not support current claims. Checklist Notes and the companion claim/source CSV map controls to references; project acceptance procedures are operating policy. Change history retains prior wording and source dates. Its observed verification date comes from saved test evidence and is not a claimed edit timestamp. Unknown dates/authorship remain Unknown. Reverify volatile platform claims before release and after provider changes; legal/privacy scope also needs qualified jurisdiction/business review. Current exact X Cards requirements remain unverified.
